claims.nodeLabel: All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO)
claims.sourceText: P.L. 117-81; P.L. 117-263; AARO FY2024 and FY2025 annual reports cite 50 U.S.C. 3373(k)
claims.text: AARO's statutory authority and annual reporting requirement are codified at 50 U.S.C. 3373, enacted through the FY2022 and FY2023 NDAAs.

Sec. 1683 was wholly replaced by sec. 6802(a) of the Intelligence Authorization Act for FY2023 (Div. F of PL 117-263), which substituted 'SEC. 1683. ESTABLISHMENT OF ALL-DOMAIN ANOMALY RESOLUTION OFFICE.' and added the 50 U.S.C. 3373(n) definitions.

Sec. 6802 of the IAA FY2023 rewrote Sec. 1683 in full, designating the 'All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office' and requiring the Director to report to the Deputy Secretary of Defense and the Principal Deputy DNI.

Sec. 1683(j) as amended requires a written Historical Record Report within 540 days, drawing on intelligence community records, oral history interviews, interviews of current and former Government officials, and classified and unclassified national archives.

Sec. 1673(a)(4)(A) requires sharing of an authorized disclosure with AARO personnel 'regardless of the classification of information contained in the disclosure or any nondisclosure agreements', unless the disclosure likely relates to a SAP or compartmented access program already 'explicitly and clearly reported to the congressional defense committees or the congressional intelligence committees, and is documented as meeting those criteria.'
PL 117-263 sec. 1673 carries the statutory note '50 USC 3373b'; enacted title 'UNIDENTIFIED ANOMALOUS PHENOMENA REPORTING PROCEDURES'; 136 Stat. 2959-2962. Approved 23 December 2022.

Sec. 1673(a)(1)(B) covers 'any activity or program by a department or agency of the Federal Government or a contractor of such a department or agency relating to unidentified anomalous phenomena, including with respect to material retrieval, material analysis, reverse engineering, research and development, detection and tracking, developmental or operational testing, and security protections and enforcement.'

Sec. 1673(b)(3)(A) requires agencies and contractors to conduct comprehensive searches of all records relating to nondisclosure orders on these subjects and to provide copies to AARO for congressional access.

Sec. 1673(b)(1)(A)-(C): an authorized disclosure 'shall not be subject to a nondisclosure agreement', 'shall be deemed to comply with any regulation or order issued under the authority of Executive Order 13526 ... or chapter 18 of the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 (42 U.S.C. 2271 et seq.)', and 'is not a violation of section 798 of title 18, United States Code'.

Sec. 1673(a)(1)(B) legislates a reporting channel for programmes involving 'material retrieval, material analysis, reverse engineering, research and development' relating to unidentified anomalous phenomena.
Sec. 1673(b)(2)(A) prohibits reprisal including revocation or suspension of security clearances or termination of employment.
Sec. 1673(b)(1)(A) provides that an authorized disclosure 'shall not be subject to a nondisclosure agreement entered into by the individual who makes the disclosure.'

claims.nodeLabel: FY2023 NDAA, Public Law 117-263 - Sec. 1673 (50 U.S.C. 3373b) UAP reporting/whistleblower protection; Div. F secs. 6802-6803 establishing AARO
claims.text: Sec. 1673(a)(4)(B) requires that within 72 hours of determining an authorized disclosure relates to 'a restricted access activity, a special access program, or a compartmented access program that has not been explicitly and clearly reported to the congressional defense committees or the congressional intelligence committees, the Secretary shall report such disclosure to such committees and the congressional leadership.' The statute thereby contemplates the existence of unreported special access programs touching UAP.

claims.nodeLabel: FY2023 NDAA, Public Law 117-263 - Sec. 1673 (50 U.S.C. 3373b) UAP reporting/whistleblower protection; Div. F secs. 6802-6803 establishing AARO
claims.text: The FY2023 NDAA carries the concealment premise in enacted text: sec. 1673(a)(1)(B) enumerates 'material retrieval, material analysis, reverse engineering' as categories of federal or contractor ACTIVITY OR PROGRAM that a person may need protection to report, and sec. 1673(b)(1)(A)-(B) voids NDAs and Atomic Energy Act restrictions for such disclosures. Congress does not write NDA-voiding and AEA-override language for activities it believes do not exist. Reasoning: the operative nouns are activity/program categories, not hypotheticals, and the remedy structure presupposes existing legal instruments suppressing disclosure.

b.label: AARO Historical Record Report, Volume II (unpublished)

edges.label: the same requirement, unmet
edges.note: Volume II answers to the same subsection (j) obligation. The statute requires a report on the historical record from 1 January 1945 to the completion of the Director's activities; Volume I states on its own concluding page that Volume II 'will be published in accordance with the date es[tablished]'. Volume II is the outstanding half of a statutory requirement, which is why the absence is on the board as a node rather than as a gap.

a.label: Sec. 6802, James M. Inhofe NDAA for FY2023 (Pub. L. 117-263) - AARO establishment, Historical Record Report and annual reports

b.label: AARO Report on the Historical Record of U.S. Government Involvement with UAP, Volume I

edges.label: the report it requires
edges.note: Subsection (j) as enacted by sec. 6802 is where this report comes from. 'Not later than 540 days after the date of the enactment of the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, the Director of the Office shall submit to the congressional defense committees, the congressional intelligence committees, and congressional leadership a written report detailing the historical record of the United States Government relating to unidentified anomalous phenomena'. The statute fixes its scope: it must 'focus on the period beginning on January 1, 1945, and ending on the date on which the Director of the Office completes activities under this subsection'.

a.label: Sec. 6802, James M. Inhofe NDAA for FY2023 (Pub. L. 117-263) - AARO establishment, Historical Record Report and annual reports

edges.label: establishes the office
edges.note: Sec. 6802 does not create AARO alongside anything: it amends section 1683 of the FY2022 NDAA (50 U.S.C. 3373) to read as a new section establishing the office. 'Not later than 120 days after the date of the enactment of the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, the Secretary of Defense, in coordination with the Director of National Intelligence, shall establish an office ... to carry out the duties of the Unidentified Aerial Phenomena Task Force, as in effect on December 26, 2021', and 'The office established under paragraph (1) shall be known as the "All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office"'. The reporting chain is set in the same subsection: the Director reports directly to the Deputy Secretary of Defense and the Principal Deputy Director of National Intelligence, and to USD(I&S) on administrative matters only. Read from the enacted text on govinfo, 22 August 2026.

a.label: Sec. 6802, James M. Inhofe NDAA for FY2023 (Pub. L. 117-263) - AARO establishment, Historical Record Report and annual reports

edges.label: rewrote 50 U.S.C. 3373 to establish AARO and to mandate the Historical Record Report
edges.note: Sec. 6802 of P.L. 117-263, enacted 23 December 2022, added subsection (j) requiring a Historical Record Report within 540 days and subsection (k) requiring joint DNI/SECDEF annual reports. This is the authority AARO itself cites for both report series, which makes it enacted law with directly observable output.
